title: Supreme Court: Barr v. Lee
summary: The District Court’s order preliminarily enjoining the executions of four federal prisoners is vacated. (No. 20A8, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 591 U.S. 979).

title: Supreme Court: Sharp v. Murphy
summary: The judgment of the Tenth Circuit is affirmed for the reasons stated in McGirt v. Oklahoma, 591 U. S. ___. (No. 17-1107, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 591 U.S. 977).

title: Supreme Court: McGirt v. Oklahoma
summary: Land in Northeastern Oklahoma reserved for the Creek Nation since the 19th century remains “Indian country” for purposes of the Major Crimes Act, which places certain crimes under federal jurisdiction if they were committed by “[a]ny Indian” within “the Indian country.” 18 U. S. C. §1153(a). (No. 18-9526, opinion by Justice Gorsuch; 591 U. S. 894).

title: Supreme Court: Trump v. Mazars USA, LLP
summary: The courts below did not take adequate account of the significant separation of powers concerns implicated by congressional subpoenas for the President’s information. (No. 19-715, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 591 U.S. 848).

title: Supreme Court: Trump v. Vance
summary: Article II and the Supremacy Clause do not categorically preclude, or require a heightened standard for, the issuance of a state criminal subpoena to a sitting President. (No. 19-635, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 591 U.S. 786).

title: Supreme Court: Our Lady of Guadalupe School v. Morrissey-Berru
summary: The First Amendment’s Religion Clauses foreclose the adjudication of the employment-discrimination claims of Catholic school teachers Morrissey-Berru and Biel. (No. 19-267, opinion by Justice Alito; 591 U.S. 732).

title: Supreme Court: Little Sisters of the Poor Saints Peter and Paul Home v. Pennsylvania
summary: The Departments of Health and Human Services, Labor, and the Treasury had authority under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act of 2010 to promulgate rules exempting employers with religious or moral objections from providing contraceptive coverage to their employees; and those rules satisfy the Administrative Procedure Act’s notice requirements. (No. 19-431, opinion by Justice Thomas; 591 U.S. 657).

title: Supreme Court: Colorado Dept. of State v. Baca
summary: The Tenth Circuit’s judgment is reversed for the reasons stated in Chiafalo v. Washington, 591 U. S. ___. (No. 19-518, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 591 U.S. 655).

title: Supreme Court: Barr v. American Assn. of Political Consultants, Inc.
summary: The Fourth Circuit’s judgment—that the robocall restriction’s government-debt exception in 47 U. S. C. §227(b)(1)(A)(iii) violates the First Amendment but is severable from the remainder of the statute—is affirmed. (No. 19-631, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 591 U.S. 610).

title: Supreme Court: Chiafalo v. Washington
summary: A State may enforce an elector’s pledge to support his party’s nominee—and the state voters’ choice—for President. (No. 19-465, opinion by Justice Kagan; 591 U.S. 578).
